scope.other_tools: Read for interface context only; vault/census have no --list interface and were not subjected to this input battery.
scope.fixture_policy: All fixture repos, copied subjects, scripts and logs are under mktemp -d -p /var/tmp roots; TMPDIR=/var/tmp for tool-created temporary files. No git fetch/push/commit/branch, no secret-shaped file reads, and no .ufo/state or .ufo/watchdog.log access.
scope.receipt_ground_truth: Fixture target bytes are introduced at a plumbing-created commit, local main and refs/remotes/origin/main point to that commit, origin/HEAD resolves main, and there are zero unpushed touching commits. No network operation establishes these simulated pushed receipts.

confirmed_defects.title: NUL bytes in --list are silently erased, authorizing a different path or receipt
confirmed_defects.root_cause: Bash read -r ignores NUL bytes. The row is validated and used only after this lossy read, so byte-invalid paths and nonmatching receipt pins become valid authorized rows without a refusal.

contradictions.contract: Fail closed on an unrepresentable path; do not delete a different pathname.
contradictions.observed: rc=0; RESULT .../victim.txt DELETED pushed; victim.txt absent; no quarantine copy remains.
contradictions.why_false_authorization: A Linux pathname cannot contain NUL. The listed invalid path is silently changed to an existing, different path instead of being rejected.

contradictions.contract: The --list receipt is an authorization pin and must match EXACTLY (tool header lines 17-22).
contradictions.observed: rc=0; RESULT .../victim.txt DELETED pushed; victim.txt absent; no quarantine copy remains.
contradictions.why_false_authorization: push<NUL>ed is not the receipt pushed, but the embedded NUL is erased before the exact-match gate. Control pin pushxed is correctly NOT-AUTHORIZED(receipt-mismatch), rc=3, file retained.

confirmed_defects.limits: The resulting real target has a genuine fixture pushed receipt. This is an input-authorization/identity defect, not a fabricated pushed receipt or a demonstrated loss of unpreserved content. The two contradictions share one NUL-erasure root cause and are not double-counted as two defects.
confirmed_defects.recommended_fix_for_implementor: Reject NUL/binary list input before any Bash line read can erase bytes, and complete structural list validation before invoking flow_one. Add both invalid-path and nonmatching-pin byte cases as regression tests. No tool edits made by S04.

observations_not_counted_as_defects.title: Structural usage error can follow completed deletions
observations_not_counted_as_defects.status: CONFIRMED-BEHAVIOR, NOT COUNTED AS FALSE DELETE
observations_not_counted_as_defects.observed: Both fresh installed-tool invocations delete victim.txt, remove the quarantine copy, then exit 2 with the malformed-row error. No SUMMARY record is emitted. A valid prefix followed by a raw tab-path row behaves the same way.
observations_not_counted_as_defects.adjudication: The prefix row itself has an exact pushed authorization, and the documented stages are per target; there is no explicit all-or-nothing batch guarantee. Therefore this is not counted as a strict false SAFE/DELETE defect. It does falsify any proposed rubric claiming exit 2 implies no mutation, and warrants eager whole-list syntax validation before mutation.

observations_not_counted_as_defects.title: Raw TSV cannot unambiguously encode arbitrary Unix filenames
observations_not_counted_as_defects.status: CONFIRMED-AMBIGUITY, NOT COUNTED AS TOOL DEFECT
observations_not_counted_as_defects.filesystem_fact: Both tab and newline are legal in Unix filenames; NUL is not. A two-column, line-oriented unquoted TSV cannot represent these filenames losslessly.
observations_not_counted_as_defects.isolated_behavior: A tab-only path serializes as three columns and exits 2; a newline-only path yields a one-column first physical row and exits 2. The real weird-named files remain present.
observations_not_counted_as_defects.combined_behavior: The existing relative path keep/good.txt<TAB>pushed<NEWLINE>keep/other.txt, naively serialized with a pushed pin, becomes two valid physical TSV records. Both independently pushed target paths are deleted (rc=0), while the intended weird-named file remains. Input bytes are indistinguishable from an intentionally authorized two-row TSV.
observations_not_counted_as_defects.adjudication: Do not call the combined case a standalone engine authorization bypass: both physical records have genuine exact receipts under the documented format. List producers must reject delimiter-bearing names, or a different framed/escaped input format must be specified.

reproduction.fresh_command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, subprocess
from pathlib import Path
q = Path('/home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/souji-shokunin/tools/souji-quarantine.sh')
v = q.parent / 'souji-verify.sh'
root = Path(subprocess.check_output(['mktemp', '-d', '-p', '/var/tmp', 'souji-r9-s04-report-repro.XXXXXX'], text=True).strip())
env = dict(os.environ, TMPDIR='/var/tmp', GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL='/dev/null', GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM='/dev/null', GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS='0', GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='S04', GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='s04@example.invalid', GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='S04', GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='s04@example.invalid', LC_ALL='C')
for key in ['GIT_DIR', 'GIT_WORK_TREE', 'GIT_INDEX_FILE', 'GIT_NAMESPACE', 'GIT_CONFIG_COUNT', 'SOUJI_QUARANTINE_ALLOW_LIVE', 'SOUJI_Q_TEST_HOOK', 'SOUJI_Q_SELFTEST_ACTIVE']:
    env.pop(key, None)
cases = [('nul-path', b'victim\x00.txt\tpushed\n', 0, False), ('nul-pin', b'victim.txt\tpush\x00ed\n', 0, False), ('wrong-pin', b'victim.txt\tpushxed\n', 3, True), ('partial-one-col', b'victim.txt\tpushed\nmalformed-row\n', 2, False), ('partial-five-col', b'victim.txt\tpushed\nbad\trow\thas\tfive\tcolumns\n', 2, False)]
for name, body, expected_rc, expected_present in cases:
    base = root / name
    repo = base / 'fleet/a-shokunin'
    subprocess.run(['git', 'init', '-q', '--template=', '--initial-branch=main', str(repo)], env=env, check=True)
    target = repo / 'victim.txt'
    target.write_text('preserved fixture bytes\n')
    def git(*args, data=None):
        return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), *args], input=data, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env, check=True).stdout.decode().strip()
    git('add', 'victim.txt')
    tree = git('write-tree')
    commit = git('commit-tree', tree, data=b'preserved\n')
    git('update-ref', 'refs/heads/main', commit)
    git('update-ref', 'refs/remotes/origin/main', commit)
    git('symbolic-ref', 'refs/remotes/origin/HEAD', 'refs/remotes/origin/main')
    listing = base / 'input.tsv'
    listing.write_bytes(body)
    ledger = base / 'ledger.tsv'
    ledger.write_text('source_path\tsource_sha256\tvault_path\tvault_sha256\n')
    child_env = dict(env, SOUJI_VERIFY_BIN=str(v), SOUJI_Q_LEDGER=str(ledger), SOUJI_Q_SHOKUNIN_ROOT=str(base / 'fleet'))
    p = subprocess.run(['bash', str(q), '--hold', '0', '--list', str(listing), str(repo)], env=child_env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, timeout=30)
    (base / 'stdout.log').write_bytes(p.stdout)
    (base / 'stderr.log').write_bytes(p.stderr)
    print(name, 'input_hex=' + body.hex(), 'rc=' + str(p.returncode), 'target_present=' + str(target.exists()))
    assert p.returncode == expected_rc and target.exists() == expected_present, name
print('fresh_fixture_root=' + str(root))
PY
